slots.title: Shallow laboratory dish holding the solution, on the ground colour
slots.prompt: Laboratory still-life photograph, one subject only. A shallow circular borosilicate glass dish, plain and entirely unmarked, sits on a smooth seamless surface of a soft pearl grey (#D8D6D4). The dish holds a shallow pool of a completely transparent, colourless liquid — water-clear and lightly viscous, visible only as refraction, edge caustics and highlight, roughly eight millimetres deep, its surface perfectly still so the rim throws a clean elliptical caustic onto the floor of the dish. Photographed from about thirty degrees above, the dish centred and filling roughly sixty percent of the frame width, the ground running out to all four edges. Colour is restricted to the ground, the glass and the liquid. A single hard key light from the upper left rakes across the subject and lays one crisp shadow down to the lower right; a soft fill lifts the core of that shadow just enough to hold detail. The look is clinical, rigorous and expensive — a research laboratory, not a spa.

slots.title: Macro study of the material itself
slots.prompt: Extreme macro photograph, one subject only, filling the frame: a flat rectangular glass microscope slide carrying a thin smear of colourless crystalline material, lit from beneath so the crystals read as bright structure against the dark of the slide's edge. Behind it, a smooth seamless surface of a soft pearl grey (#D8D6D4) shows only at the very edges of the frame. Focus falls off steeply with depth, so the nearest structure is razor sharp and the rest dissolves. Colour is restricted to the ground and the material. A single hard key light from the upper left rakes across the subject and lays one crisp shadow down to the lower right; a soft fill lifts the core of that shadow just enough to hold detail. The look is clinical, rigorous and expensive — a research laboratory, not a spa.

slots.title: Glass pipette releasing a single droplet
slots.prompt: Laboratory still-life photograph, one subject only. A slender straight glass pipette, plain and entirely unmarked, enters from the top of the frame and hangs vertically, its drawn tip at about the upper third. A single pendant droplet of completely clear colourless liquid hangs from the tip, elongated and about to fall, caught sharp. Behind it a smooth seamless surface of a soft pearl grey (#D8D6D4) runs out to all four edges. The pipette occupies a narrow vertical band at the centre and the ground is otherwise unbroken. Colour is restricted to the ground, the glass and the liquid. A single hard key light from the upper left rakes across the subject and lays one crisp shadow down to the lower right; a soft fill lifts the core of that shadow just enough to hold detail. The look is clinical, rigorous and expensive — a research laboratory, not a spa.
